lead: Alfred Russel Wallace: Island Life (1880, Gutenberg #32021) footnote 'what I now consider the erroneous doctrine that actual glacial epochs recurred each 10,500 years' vs his 1869/1870 papers; also Celebes ('I now look upon Celebes as ...')
reason: The footnote is a real retraction but the early statement is in a BAAS paper (1869) and a Nature article (1870) that are not on Gutenberg; his Geographical Distribution of Animals (1876, Gutenberg #56506, found this time) has no Croll/10,500-year passage (grepped), so no early text of his own; the Celebes remark in Island Life is only 'a solution ... more simple than any previously proposed', not a retraction.

lead: Andrew Lang: Making of Religion (1898, 2nd ed. 1900, Gutenberg #12353) withdrawals vs Myth, Ritual and Religion (1887) / Custom and Myth (1884)
reason: The Gutenberg Myth, Ritual and Religion (#2832, #36794) is the 1899 revised edition (chapters xi-xii rewritten, original passages only in notes), so no clean 1887 text; Lang's 1900 preface withdraws a statement ('Darumulun never died') from the SAME book's earlier edition, and Custom and Myth (1884, #14080) takes no explicit stand on the ghost theory of savage gods.

lead: Joseph Hooker: Introductory Essay to the Flora of Tasmania (1859) vs Introductory Essay to the Flora of New Zealand (1853)
reason: The 1859 essay explicitly says the 1853 essay advanced the immutability of species only as propositions 'which I refrained from endorsing as articles of my own creed', and the 1853 text (archive.org OCR) merely lists rival views, so there is no early passage in which Hooker himself asserts the old view.

lead: Joseph Priestley: Memoirs (Gutenberg #75111) vs an Arian-period work
reason: Rutt's 1817 Works (archive.org, 1.5 MB volumes) were searched again: vol. II (Institutes, written 1772) and vols IV-VI contain no clean Arian-period statement in his own words that predates the Socinian turn; the 1761-68 tracts were not located in the volumes tried (II, IV, V, VI, VIII, IX).

lead: E. B. Pusey: Historical Enquiry into the Rationalist Character of German Theology (1828) vs its 1830 Part II / reply to Rose
reason: Part I (1828) is on archive.org (historicalenquir00puse) but I could not find a Part II or any text in which Pusey himself retracts the Part I view; stopped.

lead: J. W. Colenso: Ten Weeks in Natal (1855) vs The Pentateuch and Book of Joshua Critically Examined (1862)
reason: The 1855 OCR (archive.org tenweeksinnatalj00cole) has only an incidental Noah remark by a Zulu, and the dli.ministry.18474 copy of the Pentateuch returned an archive 404 page; no early statement of his own belief in the Flood/Pentateuch was found.

lead: W. S. Jevons: Principles of Science (Gutenberg #74864) on exclusive disjunction vs Pure Logic (1864)
reason: The Gutenberg text is the 2nd edition; its retraction ('In the first edition of this work (vol. i., p. 81), I took ... exclusive alternatives') concerns an earlier edition of the same work, and Pure Logic (1864) is not on Gutenberg.

lead: George Boole: Laws of Thought (1854) vs Mathematical Analysis of Logic (1847)
reason: Gutenberg #15114 and #36884 returned 404 pages for every file path tried (txt, html, 8-bit); no text obtained.

lead: Hugh Miller: Footprints of the Creator (1849, Gutenberg #67527) and The Old Red Sandstone (1841, #63923) as the early work for the Testimony of the Rocks preface
reason: The Old Red Sandstone says nothing on the days of creation, and Footprints already contains the transitional footnote ('I have begun to suspect' that the days were protracted); the early Chalmers-gap statement was found instead in First Impressions of England (1847), which is used.

lead: Tolstoy (What Is Art?, Kingdom of God Is Within You, Gutenberg #43409/#64908), Du Bois (Darkwater), Galton (Inquiries into Human Faculty), Sidgwick (Methods of Ethics prefaces), John Fiske (Idea of God), Bellamy (Equality), Southey (Colloquies), Hitchcock, Dawson, Gray, Mivart
reason: Downloaded and grepped for retraction phrases ('formerly held', 'I was wrong', 'my former opinion', 'I no longer'); either no retraction of a stated thesis (Tolstoy, Du Bois, Galton, Fiske, Bellamy, Southey, Hitchcock, Dawson, Mivart), or the retraction is in a new edition of the same work (Sidgwick), or concerns a fact rather than a thesis (Gray, quoting Darwin's Origin).

lead: Ruskin: other theses (Seven Lamps, Stones of Venice, Arrows of the Chace, Elements of Drawing, Queen of the Air, Eagle's Nest, Time and Tide, Praeterita); Modern Painters II on Venetian art
reason: Grepped ten later Ruskin works on Gutenberg for self-corrections: only incidental ones (a mistaken remark on Pre-Raphaelite 'Romanizing tendencies' inside one 1851 letter; 'I formerly supposed' about a Tintoret colour). The one usable retraction found is the 1860 preface to Modern Painters vol. V on Rubens (case kept, flagged for the same-title issue); the Venetian-art 'sensual' retraction in the same preface was not used because it duplicates that preface.

The only pre-1930 English version is Pilkington's in NPNF vol. I, which I could not find as a separate text in the CCEL table of contents, and early works (Soliloquies, Against the Academics) have no clean pre-1930 English edition; not pursued.

lead: Thomas Jefferson: Notes on the State of Virginia (1785) vs letters to Banneker (1791) / Grégoire (1809) on the intelligence of Black Americans
reason: Jefferson's 1809 letter only says he would be glad to see his 'doubts' refuted; Monticello and historians present it as a hedge, not a change of mind, so the direction is not documented well enough; not used.

lead: Wordsworth: Prelude Books X-XII vs the Letter to the Bishop of Llandaff (already in dropped3)
reason: Instead the Letter (1793) was paired with Wordsworth's own prose Letter to a Friend (1821) in Grosart's Prose Works (Gutenberg #16550), which is plain prose; kept as a case.

lead: Edmund Burke, Paine, Gibbon, Comte, Harriet Martineau, Leslie Stephen, Kingsley, Carlyle, M. Arnold, Haeckel, Royce, Mach, Marshall, Henry George, Paley, T. Arnold, Asa Gray
reason: Availability check or short search only: no documented retraction of a specific thesis in the author's own later text (Burke, Paine, Gibbon, Stephen, Carlyle, Arnold, Haeckel, Mach, Marshall, George, Paley, Gray), or the later work is not on Gutenberg and no clean OCR was found (Comte, Martineau, Royce); a few web searches for retractions in prefaces turned up no new leads.
